datasource_item.source_question_text:
A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0. [incorrect]
B. 𝑣0 cos𝜃. [correct]
C. 𝑣0 sin𝜃. [incorrect]
D. 0. [incorrect]
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
A diver launches from the water with speed v0 at an angle θ above the horizontal. What is the diver’s speed at the maximum height of the trajectory (neglect air resistance)?
A. v0. This is incorrect because the vertical component decreases to zero, so the speed generally drops from its initial value. [incorrect]
B. v0 cos θ. This is correct because at the top the vertical velocity is zero while the horizontal component remains v0 cos θ. [correct]
C. v0 sin θ. This is incorrect because v0 sin θ is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at maximum height. [incorrect]
D. 0. This is incorrect because only the vertical component becomes zero at the top, not the horizontal motion. [incorrect]

datasource_item.source_question_text:
An object can escape a planet with radius R and mass M at an escape speed given by 𝑣 = √2𝐺𝑀⁄𝑅, where 𝐺 is the universal gravitational constant. Based on this expression for escape speed, which of the following statements is correct?
A. A heavier object requires a higher speed to escape from the planet. [incorrect]
B. A lighter object requires a lower speed to escape from the planet. [incorrect]
C. An object requires a higher speed to escape from a planet with smaller mass and a larger radius. [incorrect]
D. An object requires a higher speed to escape from a planet with greater mass and a smaller radius. [correct]
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
An object can escape a planet with radius R and mass M at an escape speed given by v = q2GM R , where G is the universal gravitational constant. Based on this expression, which statement is correct?
A. A more massive spacecraft needs a higher speed to escape from the same planet. This is incorrect because the escape-speed formula depends on the planet’s M and R, not the escaping object’s mass. [incorrect]
B. A less massive spacecraft needs a lower speed to escape from the same planet. This is incorrect for the same reason: escape speed is independent of the object’s mass in this model. [incorrect]
C. Escape speed is higher for a planet with smaller mass and larger radius. This is incorrect because both smaller M and larger R reduce M/R and thus reduce v. [incorrect]
D. Escape speed is higher for a planet with larger mass and smaller radius. This is correct because v ∝ p M/R, so increasing M and decreasing R both increase escape speed. [correct]
